text: Which statutory body is legally mandated by the Federal Government of Nigeria to regulate the training, registration, and licensing of Community Health Practitioners?

options.A: National Association of Community Health Practitioners of Nigeria (NACHPN)
options.B: Community Health Practitioners Registration Board of Nigeria (CHPRBN)
options.C: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN)
options.D: National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA)

explanation: The Community Health Practitioners Registration Board of Nigeria (CHPRBN) is the regulatory body established by law (originally Decree No. 61 of 1992, now LFN Cap C19 2004) to regulate training, registration, and practice. NACHPN is the professional association, not the regulatory board.

text: Which of the following professional associations is the umbrella body representing the welfare and interests of Community Health Practitioners in Nigeria?

options.A: National Association of Community Health Practitioners of Nigeria (NACHPN)
options.B: Community Health Practitioners Registration Board of Nigeria (CHPRBN)
options.C: Medical and Dental Consultants' Association of Nigeria (MDCAN)
options.D: National Association of Nigeria Nurses and Midwives (NANNM)

explanation: NACHPN is the voluntary professional association representing CHEWs, JCHEWs, and CHOs across Nigeria. CHPRBN, on the other hand, is the government regulatory agency.

text: What is the primary purpose of the Oath of Office taken by a newly graduated Community Health Extension Worker (CHEW) during induction?

options.A: To secure a promotion to the next civil service grade level
options.B: To pledge commitment to ethical practice, patient confidentiality, and preservation of life
options.C: To register as a life member of the local political ward committee
options.D: To exempt the practitioner from paying income taxes to the State Ministry of Health

explanation: The Oath of Office is a solemn pledge administered by the CHPRBN during licensing to ensure practitioners commit to ethical codes, protect patient confidentiality, and prioritize the lives and health of their clients.

text: Under the CHPRBN Act, Cap C19 Laws of the Federation of Nigeria (LFN) 2004, what constitutes professional negligence by a CHEW?

options.A: Referring a patient with severe pre-eclampsia to a General Hospital
options.B: Failing to administer a prescribed drug within the specified time or standard of care, leading to patient harm
options.C: Advising a patient to take oral rehydration salts for mild diarrhea
options.D: Participating in an LGA-wide immunisation campaign during weekend hours

explanation: Professional negligence occurs when a practitioner fails to exercise the standard of care that a reasonably prudent and trained CHEW would exercise, leading directly to patient harm, injury, or death.

text: A pharmaceutical representative offers a CHEW a direct cash incentive of ₦50,000 to promote and prioritize their brand of antimalarial over generic ACTs in a primary health clinic. What is the ethically correct response according to the CHPRBN Code of Conduct?

options.A: Accept the money but continue prescribing the generic drugs
options.B: Politely decline the offer to avoid conflict of interest and preserve professional integrity
options.C: Accept the money and share it with the Officer-in-Charge (OIC)
options.D: Request that the money be paid to the facility's drug revolving fund account

explanation: The CHPRBN Code of Conduct strictly prohibits accepting personal financial inducements, bribes, or gifts from pharmaceutical companies, as it compromises objective clinical judgment, cost-effective prescribing, and patient safety.

text: A CHEW working at a primary health facility starts dating a patient currently receiving TB treatment under their supervision. How does this behavior stand under the professional code of ethics?

options.A: It is acceptable as long as it does not interfere with the patient's drug compliance
options.B: It is a clear breach of professional boundaries and constitutes ethical misconduct
options.C: It is acceptable if the patient's family approves of the relationship
options.D: It is permitted because TB treatment is conducted under the DOTS outpatient strategy

explanation: Maintaining clear professional boundaries is vital. Engaging in sexual or romantic relationships with patients compromises objectivity, abuses the power dynamic between provider and patient, and constitutes serious professional misconduct.

text: While reviewing clinic registers, a CHEW discovers that a colleague is recording fictitious immunisation data to meet LGA targets. What is the most appropriate action to take?

options.A: Ignore the finding to maintain team harmony and protect the colleague
options.B: Report the misconduct confidentially to the Officer-in-Charge or the LGA PHC Coordinator
options.C: Help the colleague write better reports to cover up the discrepancies
options.D: Confront the colleague publicly during the community morning assembly

explanation: Falsifying data compromises public health planning and resource allocation. Professional ethics demand that such misconduct be reported through appropriate administrative channels (OIC or LGA Coordinator) to protect data integrity.

text: Under CHPRBN guidelines, how often are Community Health Practitioners in Nigeria required to renew their practicing licenses?

options.A: Annually
options.B: Every two years
options.C: Every three years
options.D: Every five years

explanation: Under the current guidelines of the Community Health Practitioners Registration Board of Nigeria, practitioners are required to renew their practicing licenses triennially (every three years), showing proof of completing mandatory continuing professional development (MCPD).

text: A practitioner is summoned before the CHPRBN Investigating Panel for allegedly performing an unsafe abortion at a private chemist shop. What is the relationship between this Panel and the Disciplinary Tribunal?

options.A: The Panel has the power to permanently strip the practitioner's license
options.B: The Panel investigates the allegation and determines if there is a prima facie case to refer to the Tribunal
options.C: The Panel acts as an appellate court for the decisions made by the Tribunal
options.D: The Panel is run by the Ministry of Justice, while the Tribunal is run by the Ministry of Health

explanation: Under the CHPRBN Act, the Investigating Panel conducts a preliminary inquiry. If they find a prima facie case of professional misconduct, the case is sent to the Disciplinary Tribunal (which functions like a court) to conduct a trial and pass judgment.

text: During a home visit, a CHEW learns that a patient with active pulmonary tuberculosis is refusing DOTS treatment and has returned to work at a local bakery. What is the ethical priority of the CHEW in this situation?

options.A: Respect the patient's absolute autonomy and keep their diagnosis confidential
options.B: Balance confidentiality with public safety by advising the patient and reporting to public health authorities for intervention
options.C: Post a notice on the bakery door warning the public about the TB risk
options.D: Prescribe and hide TB drugs in the patient's daily meals without their knowledge

explanation: While patient confidentiality is an ethical obligation, it is not absolute. In situations of public health threats (like infectious active TB in a food handler), the practitioner must prioritize public safety by reporting to the appropriate disease control officer.

text: According to the Community Health Practitioners Registration Board of Nigeria Act, Cap C19 LFN 2004, which of the following is correct regarding the legal status of decisions made by the CHPRBN Disciplinary Tribunal?

options.A: Decisions are merely advisory and must be approved by the Minister of Health
options.B: Decisions have the status of a High Court judgment and can be appealed directly to the Court of Appeal
options.C: Decisions must be ratified by the President of Nigeria before enforcement
options.D: Decisions can only be appealed through the LGA PHC Department

explanation: Under the CHPRBN Act, the Disciplinary Tribunal is a quasi-judicial body. Its decisions carry the same weight as a High Court judgment, and appeals against its judgments go directly to the Court of Appeal of Nigeria.

text: A Junior CHEW administered an intramuscular injection of a drug outside the Standing Orders to a child at a Health Post, resulting in sciatic nerve injury. The Officer-in-Charge (OIC), who is a Senior CHEW, did not authorize the injection but was present in the facility and failed to supervise. Who bears the primary legal liability under the doctrine of professional negligence?

options.A: Only the Junior CHEW, because they performed the physical act
options.B: Only the OIC, because they are the administrative head of the facility
options.C: Both the Junior CHEW for direct negligence, and the OIC under vicarious or supervisory liability
options.D: Neither, as it is considered an occupational hazard covered by local health insurance

explanation: The Junior CHEW is liable for executing a procedure beyond their clinical boundaries (as defined in the Standing Orders). The OIC is also liable for negligent supervision since they were present and failed to ensure standard care and protocol compliance.

text: Under the provisions of the CHPRBN Act, Cap C19 LFN 2004, if a person who is not registered on the Board's register practices or holds themselves out as a registered Community Health Practitioner, what is the legal consequence?

options.A: They are only liable to pay a small administrative fine of ₦5,000 to the LGA
options.B: They commit a criminal offense and are liable upon conviction to a fine, imprisonment, or both
options.C: They are automatically banned from applying to study community health in the future
options.D: They will be reprimanded by the local Ward Development Committee

explanation: Section 17 of the CHPRBN Act (LFN Cap C19 2004) makes it a criminal offense for unregistered persons to practice or pretend to be registered practitioners. Conviction carries penalties of a fine, imprisonment, or both.

text: A CHEW is accused of accepting a bribe of ₦100,000 to issue a false medical certificate of fitness. The case is brought before the CHPRBN Disciplinary Tribunal. Which of the following penalties can the Tribunal legally impose under the CHPRBN Act?

options.A: Sentencing the practitioner to a maximum of 5 years in a federal correctional center
options.B: Striking the practitioner's name off the register, suspending registration, or issuing a reprimand
options.C: Seizing the practitioner's personal properties and assets
options.D: Dissolving the Ward Development Committee of the practitioner's community

explanation: Under the CHPRBN Act, the Disciplinary Tribunal can impose professional sanctions: striking the name off the register (permanent revocation of license), suspending the practitioner from practice for a set period, or issuing a formal reprimand. It cannot sentence a person to prison; that is reserved for criminal courts.

text: Which of the following documents serves as the legal defense of a CHEW when accused of negligence for performing a clinical procedure that led to an adverse outcome, provided they followed it strictly?

options.A: The Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
options.B: The National Standing Orders for Community Health Practitioners in Nigeria
options.C: The Civil Service Rules of the State Government
options.D: The NACHPN Constitution

explanation: The National Standing Orders are the legally approved clinical guidelines defining the scope of practice and clinical steps for Community Health Practitioners. Following it exactly and documenting the care provides a complete defense against allegations of malpractice.

text: When conducting a counseling session for a woman seeking family planning, what does the first 'G' in the GATHER framework represent?

options.A: Give the client options
options.B: Greet the client warmly
options.C: Gather information about the client
options.D: Go over the side effects

explanation: The GATHER counseling framework starts with 'Greet' the client. This builds rapport and trust, which are critical for effective clinical counseling.

text: Which of the following is a non-verbal communication cue that indicates active listening by a healthcare provider?

options.A: Looking at the clinic wall clock repeatedly
options.B: Maintaining appropriate eye contact and nodding head gently
options.C: Writing in the register while the patient is speaking
options.D: Crossing arms and leaning backward

explanation: Non-verbal communication like making eye contact, nodding, and leaning forward shows the patient that they are being listened to, facilitating therapeutic dialogue.

text: When correcting an error in a patient's case notes or register, what is the best practice for a CHEW to ensure documentation integrity?

options.A: Apply corrector fluid (Tipp-Ex) over the mistake and write on it
options.B: Scribble heavily over the error until it is completely unreadable
options.C: Draw a single line through the error, write the correct information, and initial it
options.D: Tear out the entire page and start writing on a new sheet

explanation: To maintain transparency and prevent suspicion of data tampering, errors in clinical records should be crossed with a single line (remaining legible), corrected, signed, and dated.

text: A CHEW is explaining the preparation of Salt-Sugar Solution (SSS) to a mother who does not speak English. What is the most effective approach to ensure she understands?

options.A: Give her a written leaflet printed in English
options.B: Speak louder in English and use hand gestures to show quantities
options.C: Explain in her local language and ask her to perform a return-demonration
options.D: Ask her to take the ingredients home and figure it out by trial

explanation: To overcome language and literacy barriers, communicating in the local dialect and having the patient physically demonstrate the preparation (return-demonstration) is the most effective way to verify understanding.

text: What are the components of the acronym 'GATHER' in the order they should be implemented during counseling?

options.A: Greet, Ask, Tell, Help, Explain, Return
options.B: Greet, Assess, Treatment, Health-educate, Evaluate, Referral
options.C: Gather, Analyze, Test, Help, Evaluate, Record
options.D: Greet, Ask, Test, Help, Educate, Return

explanation: The GATHER model stands for Greet the client, Ask the client about their needs, Tell the client about their options, Help the client choose, Explain how to use the chosen method, and schedule a Return visit.

text: During a health talk on exclusive breastfeeding, a CHEW notices that several mothers are looking away, yawning, and talking among themselves. What does this feedback suggest to the CHEW?

options.A: The mothers are tired and the CHEW should speak louder
options.B: The communication has failed due to a lack of interest, and the method needs to be interactive
options.C: The mothers are fully understanding the information and require no further explanation
options.D: The venue is too small and lacks proper ventilation

explanation: Yawning and distractions are indicators of feedback showing low interest. The CHEW should adapt by changing the communication method to be more engaging, such as using songs, stories, or group discussions.

text: A patient presents with signs of severe pneumonia. The CHEW decides to refer the patient to a tertiary facility. Which of the following is the most important communication tool to accompany the patient?

options.A: A verbal message sent through the patient's relative
options.B: A detailed written referral letter stating history, vital signs, treatment given, and reason for referral
options.C: The patient's entire personal NHMIS register sheet
options.D: A text message to the local government health coordinator

explanation: A formal, clear referral letter ensures clinical handover. It communicates what the CHEW observed and did (like initial doses of antibiotics), which is vital for the receiving hospital's triage.

text: Which of the following communication methods is most suitable for changing deeply rooted cultural beliefs and myths about child immunization in a conservative community?

options.A: Distributing posters written in English at the market square
options.B: Holding a structured community dialogue with traditional and religious leaders
options.C: Broadcasting radio jingles on national television
options.D: Writing an official letter of complaint to the Local Government Chairman

explanation: Community dialogue involving key local influencers (traditional leaders, religious figures) fosters trust, addresses concerns, and secures community endorsement, which is necessary to dismantle health myths.

text: In communication, the term 'noise' refers to which of the following?

options.A: Only the physical loud sound from a generator next to the clinic
options.B: Any factor (physical, physiological, or psychological) that distorts or interferes with the transmission of a message
options.C: The feedback given by the patient at the end of the session
options.D: The local language spoken by the community members

explanation: In communication theory, 'noise' represents any barrier to message delivery, whether physical (noise, distance), physiological (hearing loss, pain), or psychological (fear, anxiety, language differences).

text: A CHEW is documenting a child's immunization details in the child register (NHMIS Form 002). Why is accurate and timely documentation considered a form of professional communication?

options.A: It is used to justify the clinic's budget to the local ward development committee
options.B: It communicates patient health history to other team members and ensures continuity of care
options.C: It is required to prove that the CHEW is physically present at the clinic daily
options.D: It serves as proof for drug purchase from private pharmaceutical vendors

explanation: Records communicate clinical information to other health workers. Poor documentation can lead to medication errors, double-dosing, or missed treatments, compromising patient safety.

text: Which of the following health education methods is most appropriate when teaching a group of adolescents about the correct use of male condoms?

options.A: A formal lecture in a classroom setting
options.B: A visual demonstration using an anatomical model, followed by a Q&A session
options.C: Handing out written booklets for them to read at home
options.D: Displaying a large poster at the entrance of the health clinic

explanation: Visual demonstration using models helps build practical skills (psychomotor domain) in an objective manner, and the Q&A session allows safe space for addressing personal questions.

text: A CHEW is counseling an illiterate mother on how to administer liquid pediatric paracetamol at home. Which communication tool will best prevent dosage errors?

options.A: A syringe marked with a colored line showing the exact level of the dose, combined with verbal verification
options.B: Writing '1 teaspoon three times daily' on the bottle label in English
options.C: Asking the mother to estimate the dose using a standard household cooking spoon
options.D: Telling the mother to give the medicine whenever the child feels warm

explanation: Illiterate clients cannot read written labels. Marked syringes or cups provide a concrete visual guide that, when verified, reduces the risk of dangerous under-dosing or over-dosing.

text: Under the National Health Management Information System (NHMIS) guidelines in Nigeria, what communication process is used to resolve discrepancies between data entered in registers and data submitted in monthly summary forms?

options.A: Data Triangulation and Auditing
options.B: Retrospective Correction
options.C: Community Verification Dialogue
options.D: Administrative Disciplinary Trial

explanation: Data triangulation and auditing compare summary reports with daily registers to resolve errors and verify data quality before sending monthly reports to the LGA.

text: During a community health dialogue regarding maternal mortality, a youth leader aggressively accuses the clinic staff of causing the death of a local woman due to negligence. How should the CHEW manage this communication breakdown?

options.A: Defend the staff aggressively and threaten to close down the health post
options.B: Listen actively without interrupting, validate their anger, and explain the facts calmly while proposing a joint review of referral bottlenecks
options.C: Ignore the youth leader and direct the speech only to the elderly chiefs present
options.D: Walk out of the meeting immediately to report the youth leader to the local police

explanation: Conflict management in community mobilization requires active listening, validating feelings (empathy), avoiding defensive arguments, and reframing the issue into collaborative action.

text: In the communication process, a CHEW uses the 'Teach-back' method to verify that a patient has understood how to take their antihypertensive medication. Which component of the communication model is the CHEW seeking to secure?

options.A: Decoding
options.B: Encoding
options.C: Feedback
options.D: Transmission

explanation: The 'Teach-back' method is a tool to obtain feedback. Feedback allows the sender (the CHEW) to evaluate if the receiver (the patient) decoded the message as intended.

text: Which tier of government in Nigeria is constitutionally responsible for the direct management and provision of primary healthcare services?

options.A: Federal Government
options.B: State Government
options.C: Local Government Area (LGA)
options.D: Ward Development Committee (WDC)

explanation: While the Federal Ministry of Health sets policies and the State coordinates, the LGA has the primary constitutional responsibility for the day-to-day operation and administration of PHC services.

text: Under the three-tier healthcare delivery system in Nigeria, which level of health facility does a General Hospital belong to?

options.A: Primary level
options.B: Secondary level
options.C: Tertiary level
options.D: Quaternary level

explanation: Secondary healthcare, which includes General Hospitals and comprehensive clinics, is managed by the State Government through the State Ministry of Health and its Hospital Management Board.

text: Which fund was established by the National Health Act of 2014 to guarantee a basic minimum package of health services to all Nigerians?

options.A: Nigeria Trust Fund (NTF)
options.B: Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF)
options.C: National Health Insurance Authority Fund (NHIAF)
options.D: Sovereign Wealth Fund (SWF)

explanation: The BHCPF was established under Section 11 of the National Health Act (NHAct 2014) to provide funding for primary health care and universal health coverage.

text: How is the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF) funded under the provisions of the National Health Act 2014?

options.A: An annual grant of ₦10 billion from the Central Bank of Nigeria
options.B: A statutory allocation of not less than 1% of the Consolidated Revenue Fund (CRF) of the Federation
options.C: A 5% tax on all imported pharmaceutical products
options.D: Direct voluntary donations from local government chairmen

explanation: The Federal Government of Nigeria is legally mandated to fund the BHCPF with a minimum of 1% of its Consolidated Revenue Fund, alongside donor contributions.

text: What was the main purpose of the Bamako Initiative (BI), adopted by African Ministers of Health including Nigeria in 1987?

options.A: To phase out local traditional medicine practices completely
options.B: To improve access to essential drugs through community-managed drug revolving funds and user fees
options.C: To build tertiary teaching hospitals in every rural local government area
options.D: To provide free healthcare for all civil servants in the state capital

explanation: The Bamako Initiative introduced community-based drug revolving funds (DRF) to resolve the chronic shortage of essential drugs in primary health clinics by allowing facilities to charge user fees and reinvest them.

text: Which administrative unit represents the operational base of the Ward Health System (WHS) implemented in Nigeria?

options.A: The Local Government Area Headquarters
options.B: The political ward
options.C: The autonomous village community
options.D: The state senatorial district

explanation: The Ward Health System utilizes the political ward as the basic unit for planning and executing primary health care services to ensure equitable coverage.

text: Which statutory agency under the Federal Ministry of Health is directly responsible for coordinating and implementing primary health care policies in Nigeria?

options.A: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
options.B: National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA)
options.C: National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
options.D: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC)

explanation: NPHCDA is the federal agency established to support state and local governments in developing and implementing primary healthcare services.

text: The State Primary Health Care Development Board (SPHCDB) was created to resolve which of the following operational challenges in Nigeria?

options.A: The lack of medical equipment in federal teaching hospitals
options.B: Fragmented management of PHC due to overlapping responsibilities between SMOH and LGAs (PHC Under One Roof)
options.C: The high cost of importing pharmaceutical raw materials
options.D: The registration and licensing of private chemist shops

explanation: Under the 'Primary Health Care Under One Roof' (PHCUOR) policy, the SPHCDB was established to unify all PHC management, funding, and staffing under a single state-level authority.

text: In the Nigerian health system, who is the political head of the Federal Ministry of Health (FMOH) responsible for national health policies?

options.A: The Permanent Secretary
options.B: The Honorable Minister of Health
options.C: The Director-General of NPHCDA
options.D: The President of the CHPRBN

explanation: The Honorable Minister of Health is the political head of the FMOH, appointed by the President, while the Permanent Secretary is the administrative head.

text: Under the Ward Health System, which community-based body is responsible for representing the community in the co-management of local PHC facilities?

options.A: Local Government Service Commission
options.B: Ward Development Committee (WDC)
options.C: NACHPN State Branch Executive Committee
options.D: Community Health Practitioners Investigating Panel

explanation: The Ward Development Committee (WDC) is comprised of local representatives, including village heads and women groups, who oversee and co-manage PHC services, fostering community participation.

text: Which of the following documents outlines the strategic direction for health development in Nigeria, updated to align with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)?

options.A: The CHPRBN Act
options.B: The National Health Policy
options.C: The Bamako Initiative Guideline
options.D: The Civil Service Rules

explanation: The National Health Policy is the guiding document that details the government's plans, priorities, and strategies for achieving universal health coverage and sustainable development goals.

text: Under the allocation formula for the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF) in Nigeria, what percentage of the fund is allocated to the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) gate for the basic minimum package of health services?
explanation: The BHCPF is split as: 50% to the NHIA gate (for purchasing a basic package of health services), 45% to the NPHCDA gate (for PHC operations, drugs, and human resources), and 5% to the Federal Ministry of Health for emergency medical treatment.

text: In Nigeria, a Comprehensive Health Centre is a referral facility at the primary care level. Under standard guidelines, it should serve a population of approximately how many people?
explanation: Under NPHCDA guidelines, a Comprehensive Health Centre is designed to serve a catchment population of about 20,000 to 50,000 people, providing wider services than a standard Primary Health Clinic.

text: Which of the following best describes the financing flow of the NPHCDA gate under the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF) directly to the facilities?

options.A: FMOH -> SMOH -> LGA -> Cash delivery to facility OIC
options.B: Central Bank of Nigeria -> Commercial Banks -> State Primary Health Care Board -> Facility Bank Account
options.C: NPHCDA -> State SPHCDB -> LGA PHC Department -> Facility Drug Store
options.D: FMOH -> Commercial Banks -> Ward Development Committee -> OIC Cash Box

explanation: Under BHCPF guidelines, funds for operational costs (decentralized facility financing) flow directly from the CBN/SPHCDB dedicated accounts to the commercial bank accounts owned and managed by the health facilities, bypassing administrative bottlenecks.

text: The 'Primary Health Care Under One Roof' (PHCUOR) initiative, a reform in the Nigerian health system, is built on how many core pillars?

options.A: 3 pillars
options.B: 5 pillars
options.C: 9 pillars
options.D: 12 pillars

explanation: PHCUOR is implemented based on 9 core pillars: Governance and Ownership, Legislation, Finance, human resources, PHC Service Delivery, Quality, Information Systems, Drugs and Logistics, and Community Participation.

text: The Alma-Ata Declaration, which established Primary Health Care as the key strategy for achieving global health goals, was adopted in what year?
explanation: The historic International Conference on Primary Health Care was held in September 1978 in Alma-Ata, USSR.

text: Which of the following is one of the original eight essential components of Primary Health Care?

options.A: Provision of specialized surgical services
options.B: Promotion of food supply and proper nutrition
options.C: Establishment of private health insurance schemes
options.D: Manufacture of high-tech diagnostic equipment

explanation: The promotion of food supply and proper nutrition is one of the core elements of PHC defined in the Alma-Ata Declaration.

text: What was the overarching global health goal associated with the 1978 Alma-Ata Declaration?

options.A: Eradication of Malaria by 2015
options.B: Health for All by the Year 2000 (HFA 2000)
options.C: Elimination of HIV/AIDS in Africa
options.D: Reducing infant mortality by two-thirds

explanation: The Alma-Ata conference set 'Health for All by the Year 2000' as the primary global target for health systems.

text: What is the primary focus of 'Selective Primary Health Care' as proposed by Walsh and Warren, in contrast to 'Comprehensive Primary Health Care'?

options.A: It targets the whole population with broad social and economic reforms
options.B: It focuses on low-cost, high-impact vertical interventions against specific high-mortality diseases
options.C: It is based on providing private healthcare services to selected wealthy individuals
options.D: It selects only urban areas for health facility development

explanation: Selective PHC focuses on cost-effective, targeted interventions (such as the GOBI-FFF framework) rather than trying to fix the entire health system or address social determinants of health.

text: A CHEW is organizing a village clean-up campaign to clear stagnant water and drain gutters. Which element of Primary Health Care does this activity represent?

options.A: Prevention and control of locally endemic diseases
options.B: Maternal and child health care
options.C: Appropriate treatment of common diseases
options.D: Provision of essential drugs

explanation: Clearing stagnant water directly prevents the breeding of mosquitoes (malaria vectors), representing a primary preventive measure for the control of locally endemic diseases.

text: The primary health clinic partners with the local government agricultural department to train mothers on cultivating home vegetable gardens. This is an example of which PHC principle?

options.A: Community participation
options.B: Intersectoral collaboration
options.C: Appropriate technology
options.D: Equitable distribution

explanation: Intersectoral collaboration involves health sectors working with other sectors (like agriculture, education, water resources) to address the root causes of poor health.

text: Which of the following descriptions best fits the concept of 'Appropriate Technology' in Primary Health Care?

options.A: Using the most expensive and latest medical equipment imported from Western countries
options.B: Using scientifically sound, adaptable, socially acceptable, and affordable methods
options.C: Relying entirely on traditional medicine practices without scientific validation
options.D: Using manual paper registers instead of electronic systems in urban areas

explanation: Appropriate technology means using methods and equipment that are scientifically valid, yet simple, cheap, and culturally acceptable (e.g., using solar-powered refrigerators in rural clinics without electricity).

text: Under the principles of PHC, what does 'Equitable Distribution' imply for resource allocation in Nigeria?

options.A: Giving equal amounts of money to all primary, secondary, and tertiary hospitals
options.B: Allocating resources preferentially to areas and populations with the greatest health needs
options.C: Concentrating high-tech services in urban centers to serve the highest density of population
options.D: Charging all patients the same user fee regardless of their financial status

explanation: Equity means fairness, which translates to directing resources to underserved rural communities and vulnerable groups rather than distributing resources equally.

text: A primary health clinic is implementing a 'Drug Revolving Fund' (DRF). How does the DRF support the 'Provision of Essential Drugs' element of PHC?

options.A: By providing free branded drugs to all patients regardless of stock level
options.B: By using revenue from drug sales to purchase new stock, ensuring continuous drug availability
options.C: By outsourcing drug supply to private local chemist shops
options.D: By restricting drug prescriptions only to children under 5 years

explanation: The DRF ensures sustainability. When patients pay a small fee for essential generic drugs, that money is used to restock, preventing the 'out-of-stock' syndrome.

text: Which level of prevention is represented by providing physical rehabilitation services to a patient who has suffered a stroke?

options.A: Primary prevention
options.B: Secondary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Quaternary prevention

explanation: Tertiary prevention focuses on rehabilitation, reducing disability, and restoring function after an established disease or injury has occurred.

text: In the Nigerian adaptation of Primary Health Care elements, which of the following was added to the original eight elements?

options.A: Cardiovascular surgery
options.B: Mental Health and Dental Health
options.C: Alternative medicine
options.D: Aerospace medicine

explanation: Nigeria expanded the original 8 elements of PHC to include Mental Health and Dental Health, recognizing their high burden and neglect at the community level.

text: During the historical evaluation of PHC, UNICEF championed the GOBI-FFF framework. What do the three 'Fs' in this framework represent?

options.A: Fever control, First aid, Fluid intake
options.B: Female education, Family spacing, Food supplementation
options.C: Folic acid, Ferrous sulfate, Family planning
options.D: Facilities, Finance, Formulation of policy

explanation: In GOBI-FFF: G = Growth monitoring, O = Oral rehydration, B = Breastfeeding, I = Immunization, F = Female education, F = Family spacing, F = Food supplementation.

text: Under the Alma-Ata Declaration, which of the following is defined as the first point of contact of individuals, the family, and community with the national health system, bringing healthcare as close as possible to where people live and work?

options.A: Secondary healthcare
options.B: Primary healthcare
options.C: Tertiary healthcare
options.D: Specialized private clinics

explanation: Primary health care constitutes the first level of contact of individuals, the family, and the community with the national health system.

text: In a rural LGA, a CHEW notices high rates of fluorosis (tooth discoloration) due to high fluoride in borehole water. The CHEW collaborates with water engineers to set up a community defluoridation unit. This intervention is an application of which PHC concepts?

options.A: Selective PHC and Tertiary Prevention
options.B: Intersectoral Collaboration and Appropriate Technology
options.C: Autocratic Leadership and Secondary Prevention
options.D: Task Shifting and Equity

explanation: Collaborating with water engineers is Intersectoral Collaboration. Using a local defluoridation unit is a practical, low-cost solution (Appropriate Technology).

text: Which of the following statements represents the core philosophical difference between the Alma-Ata vision of PHC and the later selective PHC model?

options.A: Alma-Ata focused on technology, while selective PHC focused on social justice
options.B: Alma-Ata viewed health as a fundamental human right requiring social change, while selective PHC viewed health as a set of specific, cost-effective biomedical targets
options.C: Alma-Ata was only for developed countries, while selective PHC was designed for Africa
options.D: Alma-Ata rejected community participation, whereas selective PHC embraced it

explanation: The Alma-Ata Declaration was comprehensive and saw health as intimately linked to social, economic, and political development. Selective PHC was a pragmatic response that focused on disease-specific, vertical packages due to economic constraints.

text: Which leadership style is most appropriate when a CHEW team must make rapid, life-saving clinical decisions during a mass casualty or cholera outbreak?

options.A: Laissez-faire leadership
options.B: Autocratic leadership
options.C: Democratic leadership
options.D: Bureaucratic leadership

explanation: During an emergency, time is critical. An autocratic (or directive) style ensures rapid execution of protocols without the delay of consultations.

text: What is the process called when a senior health worker assigns a task to a subordinate while maintaining ultimate responsibility for the outcome?

options.A: Task shifting
options.B: Delegation
options.C: Appraisal
options.D: Supervision

explanation: Delegation is the transfer of authority to perform a specific task to another person, though the delegator remains accountable.

text: Within a multidisciplinary primary health care team at a Comprehensive Health Centre, who is typically the clinical lead for medical services?

options.A: The Pharmacy Technician
options.B: The Medical Officer of Health
options.C: The Junior CHEW
options.D: The Ward Development Committee Chairman

explanation: The Medical Officer of Health (doctor) is the clinical lead, managing complex cases and leading the clinical team.

text: What does 'Task Shifting' mean in the context of human resources for health in Nigeria?

options.A: Moving health workers from rural clinics to urban general hospitals
options.B: The rational redistribution of clinical tasks from highly qualified health workers to lesser-trained ones to maximize resources
options.C: Replacing all medical doctors in the country with community health practitioners
options.D: Alternating morning and night shifts among nurses and CHEWs

explanation: Task shifting (and task sharing) allows cadres like CHEWs to perform clinical procedures (such as implant insertion or newborn resuscitation) traditionally reserved for doctors/midwives, expanding access in underserved areas.

text: Two JCHEWs are having a conflict over who should handle weekend duty shifts, affecting clinic operations. What is the best initial step for the Officer-in-Charge to resolve this?

options.A: Report both workers to the police for disturbing public peace
options.B: Facilitate a meeting between both parties to discuss their concerns and agree on a fair, rotating duty schedule
options.C: Suspend both workers indefinitely without pay
options.D: Take over all weekend shifts herself and ignore the workers

explanation: A collaborative conflict resolution approach involves open communication, finding the root cause, and negotiating a mutually acceptable solution.

text: What is the primary characteristic of 'Supportive Supervision' in a primary health care setting?

options.A: Finding faults and recommending administrative queries for staff
options.B: A collaborative process of joint problem-solving, mentoring, and on-the-job training to improve performance
options.C: Conducting unannounced inspections to catch workers who are absent
options.D: Directly taking over all clinic tasks and ignoring the resident staff

explanation: Supportive supervision focuses on guiding, teaching, and encouraging staff rather than punishing them, which improves motivation and quality of care.

text: Which of the following is a non-monetary motivator that can improve the performance and retention of CHEWs in remote communities?

options.A: Paying a ₦20,000 cash bonus every week
options.B: Providing comfortable, rent-free staff quarters at the health facility
options.C: Awarding certificates of excellence and sponsoring their participation in a national conference
options.D: Reducing the daily working hours to 2 hours per day

explanation: Non-monetary motivators like recognition, awards, and professional development (sponsoring conferences) enhance job satisfaction and career growth.

text: In Tuckman's stages of team development, what is the 'Norming' stage characterized by?

options.A: Conflict and disagreement over roles and tasks
options.B: Agreement on team goals, mutual respect, and establishment of cooperative rules
options.C: High performance and autonomous task execution
options.D: Initial anxiety and polite introductions among members

explanation: In the 'Norming' stage, conflicts are resolved, group cohesion develops, and team members establish rules and respect for one another's roles.

text: Why is a routine performance appraisal essential for a CHEW working in a primary health clinic?

options.A: To justify reducing the worker's salary
options.B: To identify performance gaps, recognize achievements, and plan for future training and career advancement
options.C: To choose who will be transferred to a remote village clinic
options.D: To replace the need for licensing examinations

explanation: Performance appraisals are constructive tools used to evaluate performance against standard goals, providing feedback and identifying developmental needs.

text: A CHEW is appointed as the Officer-in-Charge (OIC) of a Primary Health Clinic. Which leadership style is best suited for day-to-day operations to foster team collaboration and buy-in?

options.A: Autocratic leadership
options.B: Democratic (Participative) leadership
options.C: Laissez-faire leadership
options.D: Coercive leadership

explanation: Democratic leadership encourages participation and input from all team members, which builds trust, alignment, and consensus in routine clinic management.

text: Under the Nigerian Task Shifting and Task Sharing Policy for Essential Health Services, which of the following clinical tasks can a trained CHEW perform independently?

options.A: Performing a Caesarean Section in the labor room
options.B: Inserting and removing subdermal contraceptive implants (e.g., Implanon)
options.C: Prescribing and initiating insulin therapy for type 1 diabetes
options.D: Performing a surgical appendectomy under general anesthesia

explanation: The Task Shifting policy authorizes trained CHEWs to insert and remove subdermal contraceptive implants and IUDs, expanding the availability of long-acting reversible contraceptives at the PHC level.

text: During an LGA-wide immunisation campaign, the PHC Coordinator delegates vaccine distribution logistics to a Senior CHEW. The Senior CHEW fails to monitor the cold chain, and vaccines spoil. Who is ultimately accountable to the State Primary Health Care Board?

options.A: Only the Senior CHEW, because they accepted the delegated task
options.B: Only the PHC Coordinator, because accountability cannot be delegated
options.C: The vaccine manufacturer, for poor product heat stability
options.D: The LGA Chairman, for lack of electricity

explanation: In management, authority can be delegated, but ultimate accountability remains with the delegator (the PHC Coordinator). The coordinator must supervise to ensure delegated tasks are completed correctly.

text: Under the Thomas-Kilmann Conflict Mode Instrument (TKI), when a leader chooses to compromise during a dispute, what is the dynamic of this resolution?

options.A: High assertiveness and low cooperation, where one party wins and the other loses
options.B: Moderate assertiveness and moderate cooperation, where both parties give up something to reach an agreement
options.C: Low assertiveness and low cooperation, where the conflict is postponed
options.D: High assertiveness and high cooperation, where a completely new win-win solution is found

explanation: Compromising is a middle-ground style where both sides make concessions to reach a quick, mutually acceptable agreement.

text: Which of the following is the most critical human resource challenge facing the implementation of the Ward Health System in rural communities in Nigeria?

options.A: A surplus of medical doctors willing to work in rural areas
options.B: Inequitable distribution and attrition (brain drain) of skilled cadres, particularly CHEWs and midwives, in rural vs. urban areas
options.C: The refusal of community members to accept modern medical services
options.D: The absence of training institutions for Community Health Practitioners

explanation: Rural PHC facilities face severe staff shortages due to the migration of skilled workers (CHEWs, nurses) to urban centers or tertiary hospitals for better pay and working conditions.

text: What is the primary difference between a 'multidisciplinary team' and an 'interdisciplinary team' in a primary health care setting?

options.A: Multidisciplinary teams have only one doctor, while interdisciplinary teams have none
options.B: Multidisciplinary teams work in parallel with distinct roles, while interdisciplinary teams integrate their processes and collaborate closely to solve complex patient problems
options.C: Multidisciplinary teams are governed by the LGA, while interdisciplinary teams are private
options.D: There is no difference; they are identical terms

explanation: In multidisciplinary care, members work individually within their scope and communicate via records. In interdisciplinary care, members integrate their skills and collaborate actively to co-manage patient care.

text: According to the National Healthcare Waste Management Guidelines in Nigeria, which colored waste bin is used for the disposal of highly infectious clinical waste (e.g., blood-soaked dressings, placenta)?

options.A: Black bin
options.B: Yellow bin
options.C: Brown bin
options.D: Green bin

explanation: Yellow bins are designated for infectious waste to prevent accidental exposure and ensure appropriate treatment (incineration).

text: In managing the drug and vaccine store of a primary health clinic, what does the rule 'FEFO' stand for?

options.A: First Entering First Outflow
options.B: First Expiry First Out
options.C: Fast Evacuation for Out-of-stock
options.D: Federal Essential Facility Order

explanation: FEFO (First Expiry, First Out) ensures that drugs or vaccines with the closest expiration dates are distributed or used first, reducing waste from expired items.

text: Which of the following is the most critical infection prevention practice to prevent cross-contamination between patients in a clinic?

options.A: Wearing double surgical masks at all times
options.B: Proper and timely hand hygiene (hand washing or rubbing)
options.C: Spraying aerosol disinfectants in the clinic every hour
options.D: Prescribing prophylactic antibiotics to all clinic visitors

explanation: Hand hygiene is the single most effective and cheapest measure to prevent the transmission of healthcare-associated infections.

text: What device is attached to a vaccine vial to show if it has been exposed to cumulative heat over time, helping a CHEW decide if the vaccine is safe to use?

options.A: Dial Thermometer
options.B: Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM)
options.C: Freeze Indicator
options.D: Stem Thermometer

explanation: A VVM is a chemical label on vaccine vials that changes color when exposed to heat over time, indicating whether the vaccine's potency has been compromised.

text: Under the WHO '5 Moments for Hand Hygiene,' which of the following represents the correct sequence or moments?

options.A: Before touching a patient, Before clean/aseptic procedures, After body fluid exposure risk, After touching a patient, After touching patient surroundings
options.B: Before entering the clinic, Before lunch, After using the toilet, After cleaning the desk, Before leaving the clinic
options.C: Before taking vital signs, After writing in the register, Before giving an injection, After washing hands, After sweeping
options.D: Before wear gloves, After wear gloves, Before touch patient, After touch patient, After touching clinical files

explanation: The WHO 5 Moments define the critical points when health workers must perform hand hygiene to protect the patient and the environment.

text: When sterilizing surgical dressings and instruments using an autoclave in a Comprehensive Health Centre, what is the standard temperature and pressure requirement?

options.A: 100°C at 5 psi for 60 minutes
options.B: 121°C at 15 psi for 15 to 20 minutes
options.C: 150°C at 30 psi for 5 minutes
options.D: 80°C at 10 psi for 45 minutes

explanation: Steam sterilization in an autoclave at 121°C (250°F) under 15 psi of pressure for 15-20 minutes is the standard to destroy all microbes including spores.

text: Which of the following is the correct protocol for disposing of used injection needles and syringes at a primary health care facility?

options.A: Recap the needle using two hands and throw it in the general waste bin
options.B: Drop them immediately into a puncture-proof safety box without recapping or bending the needle
options.C: Wash the needle with disinfectant and store it in a plastic bag for reuse
options.D: Throw them directly into the yellow plastic waste bag

explanation: Needles must never be recapped, bent, or broken to avoid needle-stick injuries. They must be dropped directly into a rigid safety box immediately after use.

text: In the national color-coding system for healthcare waste, what type of waste should be disposed of in the 'Black' bin?

options.A: Highly infectious waste like dressings and tissue
options.B: General, non-hazardous household waste (e.g., office paper, food wrappers, empty boxes)
options.C: Expired pharmaceutical drugs and heavy metals
options.D: Sharps like needles and blades

explanation: Black bins are for non-hazardous or general domestic waste that does not require special treatment before disposal.

text: How should freeze-sensitive vaccines, such as the Pentavalent and Hepatitis B vaccines, be arranged in a front-opening vaccine refrigerator?

options.A: In the freezer compartment to maximize cooling
options.B: On the middle or lower shelves, away from the evaporator plate/freezer compartment
options.C: Directly touching the ice packs at the bottom of the fridge
options.D: In the door pockets of the refrigerator

explanation: Freezing destroys the potency of vaccines containing aluminum adjuvant. They must be kept in the middle or lower shelves where the temperature is maintained between +2°C and +8°C without freezing.

text: What is the purpose of maintaining a 'Bin Card' (Stock Card) for every item in the health facility store?

options.A: To record the names of patients who received the drugs
options.B: To track the movement (receipts, issues, and balance) of each stock item at the storage point
options.C: To calculate the monthly salary of the storekeeper
options.D: To show the clinical indications of the drug

explanation: Bin cards are kept at the point of storage to provide an up-to-date record of stock levels, transactions, and batch details for each item.

text: A primary health clinic is preparing its Emergency Preparedness Plan. What is the priority step for managing a sudden outbreak of Lassa fever in the community?

options.A: Establish an isolation area, secure PPE, train staff on IPC protocols, and notify the LGA disease surveillance officer immediately
options.B: Tell all staff to stay at home until the outbreak is declared over by the Governor
options.C: Refer all patients with any fever to the federal teaching hospital without examination
options.D: Distribute antibiotics to all houses in the community

explanation: Emergency response for highly infectious diseases (viral hemorrhagic fevers) requires immediate isolation, use of personal protective equipment, staff sensitization, and prompt reporting.

text: Which of the following methods is most appropriate for sanitizing a metal dressing trolley surface contaminated with blood during a procedure?

options.A: Wiping the surface with clean tap water and a dry cloth
options.B: Disinfecting with a 0.5% chlorine solution and allowing it to air dry
options.C: Pouring boiling water over the trolley
options.D: Spraying the trolley with insecticide

explanation: Blood spills and contaminated clinical surfaces should be cleaned and disinfected with a 0.5% chlorine solution (or an appropriate hospital-grade disinfectant) to kill blood-borne pathogens.

text: A CHEW needs to prepare a 0.5% chlorine solution for environmental decontamination using a commercial liquid bleach containing 5% active chlorine. What is the correct ratio of bleach to water to prepare this solution?

options.A: 1 part bleach to 1 part water
options.B: 1 part bleach to 9 parts water
options.C: 1 part bleach to 19 parts water
options.D: 1 part bleach to 99 parts water

explanation: Formula: (% Concentrate / % Dilute) - 1 = Parts of Water. Here, (5% / 0.5%) - 1 = 10 - 1 = 9 parts of water. So, 1 part of 5% bleach mixed with 9 parts of water yields a 0.5% chlorine solution.

text: In the cold chain, what is the 'Shake Test' used for by a Community Health Practitioner?

options.A: To check if a liquid vaccine has expired
options.B: To determine if a freeze-sensitive vaccine (like Pentavalent) has been damaged by accidental freezing
options.C: To mix the dry powder of a BCG vaccine with its diluent
options.D: To verify if the vaccine refrigerator has enough refrigerant gas

explanation: The shake test is performed when freeze-sensitive vaccines are suspected to have frozen. If frozen, the structure of the adjuvant is altered, and it precipitates faster than non-frozen vaccine when shaken. This is observed by comparing sedimentation rates.

text: According to standard infection prevention guidelines, what is the correct order of donning (putting on) Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) before managing a highly infectious patient?

options.A: Gloves -> Gown -> Mask -> Goggles
options.B: Gown -> Mask -> Goggles -> Gloves
options.C: Mask -> Goggles -> Gown -> Gloves
options.D: Gloves -> Mask -> Goggles -> Gown

explanation: The recommended sequence for donning PPE is: Gown, followed by Mask or Respirator, then Goggles or Face Shield, and finally Gloves. This ensures maximum coverage and secure fit of each item.

text: According to the guidelines of the Federal Ministry of Health (FMOH) in Nigeria, what is the ideal gestational age for a pregnant woman to register (book) for Antenatal Care (ANC)?

options.A: Before 12 weeks of gestation (first trimester)
options.B: Between 16 and 20 weeks of gestation
options.C: At 28 weeks of gestation (third trimester)
options.D: Only when labor pains or complications begin

explanation: The FMOH and WHO recommend early booking before 12 weeks of gestation (first trimester). Early registration allows for baseline maternal investigations (Hb, blood group, genotype, retroviral screening), accurate gestational age estimation, detection of pre-existing health conditions, and early administration of routine prophylaxes like folic acid and tetanus toxoid.

text: According to the updated WHO Antenatal Care (ANC) model adopted by the FMOH in Nigeria, what is the minimum number of ANC contacts recommended during an uncomplicated pregnancy?

options.A: 4 contacts
options.B: 6 contacts
options.C: 8 contacts
options.D: 12 contacts

explanation: In 2016, WHO updated the focused ANC model (which recommended 4 visits) to the new 8-contact model to improve the quality of care and reduce perinatal mortality. This has been adopted by the FMOH in Nigeria. The first contact should happen before 12 weeks, followed by contacts at 20, 26, 30, 34, 36, 38, and 40 weeks.

text: Which of the following symptoms in a pregnant woman is classified as a key danger sign that requires immediate referral by a Community Health Extension Worker (CHEW)?

options.A: Mild morning sickness in the first trimester
options.B: Vaginal bleeding of any amount
options.C: Slight swelling of the ankles at the end of the day
options.D: Increased frequency of urination without pain

explanation: Vaginal bleeding during pregnancy is a critical obstetric danger sign that may indicate threatened abortion, placenta praevia, or abruptio placentae, requiring immediate referral to a facility with Emergency Obstetric Care (EmOC). Mild morning sickness, physiological ankle oedema, and urinary frequency are common discomforts of pregnancy.

text: What is the threshold haemoglobin (Hb) level below which a pregnant woman in Nigeria is diagnosed with anaemia according to the Federal Ministry of Health (FMOH) guidelines?
explanation: According to the FMOH and WHO guidelines, anaemia in pregnancy is defined as a haemoglobin concentration of less than 11.0 g/dL. Anaemia increases the risk of maternal hemorrhage, preterm delivery, low birth weight, and perinatal mortality.

text: A 26-year-old pregnant woman at 26 weeks gestation presents to a Primary Health Post. Her blood pressure is 150/95 mmHg, and a dipstick urinalysis shows 2+ protein. She has no headache or visual disturbances. What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.A: Gestational hypertension
options.B: Chronic hypertension
options.C: Pre-eclampsia
options.D: Eclampsia

explanation: Pre-eclampsia is defined as new-onset hypertension (BP >= 140/90 mmHg) after 20 weeks of gestation, accompanied by significant proteinuria (1+ or more on dipstick). If generalized seizures occur in this setting, it is classified as eclampsia.

text: Under the National Malaria Elimination Programme (NMEP) guidelines in Nigeria, which drug is administered as Intermittent Preventive Treatment of malaria in pregnancy (IPTp), and at what gestational age should it commence?

options.A: Chloroquine, starting at 6 weeks of gestation
options.B: Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine (SP), starting at 13 weeks of gestation (second trimester)
options.C: Artemether-Lumefantrine, starting at 28 weeks of gestation
options.D: Quinine, starting at booking

explanation: IPTp-SP is the national standard for malaria prevention in pregnancy. It is initiated in the second trimester, at or after 13 weeks of gestation (after quickening / fetal movements are felt), to avoid teratogenic risks in the first trimester. It is administered as a directly observed therapy (DOT) in the clinic.

text: What is the correct spacing and minimum number of doses of Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine (SP) for IPTp that a pregnant woman should receive under Nigerian guidelines?

options.A: At least 2 weeks apart, minimum of 2 doses
options.B: At least 4 weeks apart, minimum of 3 doses
options.C: Every 2 months, maximum of 2 doses
options.D: Weekly, until delivery

explanation: The FMOH guidelines recommend that pregnant women receive a minimum of 3 doses of SP, with each dose administered at least 4 weeks (one month) apart, up to the time of delivery. This ensures continuous protective levels of the drug in the placenta.

text: To effectively prevent neural tube defects such as spina bifida in the developing fetus, what is the standard daily dose of folic acid recommended for a pregnant woman starting from booking?

options.B: 5.0 mg
options.D: 100 mcg

explanation: The standard daily dose of folic acid for routine prevention of neural tube defects is 0.4 mg (400 mcg). However, women with a high risk or previous history of neural tube defects should be prescribed a therapeutic dose of 5.0 mg daily.

text: During a routine physical examination of a pregnant woman at a Primary Health Clinic, a CHEW palpates the fundus at the level of the maternal umbilicus. What is the estimated gestational age of the pregnancy?

options.A: 12 to 14 weeks
options.B: 16 to 18 weeks
options.C: 20 to 22 weeks
options.D: 28 to 30 weeks

explanation: At 20 to 22 weeks of gestation, the fundus of the uterus is typically palpable at the level of the umbilicus. Prior to this, the fundus is at the symphysis pubis at 12 weeks and midway between the symphysis pubis and umbilicus at 16 weeks.

text: In Nigeria, what is the recommended daily oral dose of elemental iron combined with folic acid (IFA) for routine prevention of gestational anaemia in areas where anaemia is a public health problem?

options.A: 30 mg elemental iron and 200 mcg folic acid
options.B: 60 mg elemental iron and 400 mcg folic acid
options.C: 120 mg elemental iron and 1 mg folic acid
options.D: 200 mg elemental iron and 5 mg folic acid

explanation: The standard daily preventive dose during pregnancy is 60 mg of elemental iron (equivalent to 300 mg of ferrous sulfate heptahydrate) and 400 mcg (0.4 mg) of folic acid. If a woman is diagnosed with clinical anaemia (Hb < 11 g/dL), the therapeutic dose is doubled (120 mg elemental iron daily).

text: Under the National PMTCT guidelines in Nigeria, what is the preferred first-line Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) regimen for a newly diagnosed HIV-positive pregnant woman?

options.A: Tenofovir + Lamivudine + Dolutegravir (TLD)
options.B: Zidovudine + Lamivudine + Nevirapine (ZLN)
options.C: Efavirenz + Abacavir + Lamivudine
options.D: Lopinavir/Ritonavir monotherapy

explanation: The current national guideline for PMTCT recommends Tenofovir (TDF) + Lamivudine (3TC) + Dolutegravir (DTG), abbreviated as TLD, as the preferred, highly effective, first-line triple therapy for HIV-positive pregnant women from the time of diagnosis, continued for life.

text: A multiparous pregnant woman at 35 weeks gestation presents with sudden-onset, severe, continuous abdominal pain, dark vaginal bleeding, and a rigid, extremely tender uterus on palpation. Fetal heart sounds are faint. What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.A: Placenta praevia
options.B: Abruptio placentae
options.C: Uterine rupture
options.D: Ectopic pregnancy

explanation: Abruptio placentae (premature separation of the placenta) typically presents with painful vaginal bleeding, uterine rigidity/tenderness, and fetal distress. Placenta praevia is characterized by painless, bright red bleeding, and the uterus remains soft and non-tender.

text: A pregnant woman with eclampsia is convulsing at a Primary Health Post. Before arranging urgent transport to a Comprehensive Health Centre or General Hospital, what is the correct pre-referral loading dose of Magnesium Sulphate (MgSO4) a CHEW should administer?

options.A: 4g IV slowly over 10-15 minutes and 10g IM (5g in each buttock)
options.B: 2g IV slowly and 4g IM in one buttock
options.C: 10g IV stat over 5 minutes
options.D: 20g IM as a single dose

explanation: The recommended loading dose of Magnesium Sulphate for eclampsia is 4g of a 20% solution IV slowly over 15 minutes, and 10g of a 50% solution IM (5g deep IM in each buttock). This is critical to control seizures and protect the maternal brain before transfer.

text: At what gestational age does abdominal palpation for fetal presentation and position (Leopold's maneuvers) become highly reliable and clinically necessary to identify malpresentation?

options.A: From 12 weeks onwards
options.B: From 20 weeks onwards
options.C: From 28 weeks onwards
options.D: Only after the onset of active labor

explanation: Leopold's maneuvers are generally performed and reliable starting from 28 weeks (third trimester) when the fetus has grown large enough to clearly distinguish the head, breech, back, and limbs. Prior to 28 weeks, the fetus has high mobility and presentation frequently changes.

text: Regarding maternal vitamin supplementation, what is the position of the Federal Ministry of Health (FMOH) on routine Vitamin A supplementation during pregnancy in Nigeria?

options.A: It is routinely given in high doses (200,000 IU) during the second trimester
options.B: It is contraindicated in high doses during pregnancy due to the risk of fetal teratogenicity
options.C: It is given at every ANC contact to prevent maternal night blindness
options.D: It is only administered if the mother is carrying twins

explanation: Routine high-dose Vitamin A supplementation (>10,000 IU daily or >25,000 IU weekly) is contraindicated in pregnancy due to the risk of birth defects (teratogenicity). However, a single high dose of 200,000 IU can be safely given to the mother in the postpartum period within 6 weeks of delivery to boost breast milk vitamin A levels.

text: According to the standard postnatal care (PNC) schedule recommended by the FMOH in Nigeria, what is the timing for the first routine check-up for a mother and newborn who delivered at home?

options.A: Within 24 hours of delivery
options.B: Exactly 1 week after birth
options.C: At 6 weeks during immunization
options.D: Only when the umbilical cord falls off

explanation: The first 24 hours postpartum are critical for both mother and newborn. Immediate PNC within 24 hours (or at 24 hours for home births) is recommended to detect early complications like postpartum haemorrhage, neonatal asphyxia, and hypothermia.

text: What is the standard ophthalmic ointment recommended by the FMOH for application to a newborn's eyes immediately after birth to prevent ophthalmia neonatorum?

options.A: 1% Tetracycline eye ointment
options.B: 0.5% Gentamicin eye drops
options.C: Chloramphenicol eye ointment
options.D: Penicillin eye drops

explanation: 1% Tetracycline eye ointment is applied to both eyes of the newborn within 1 hour of birth to prevent ophthalmia neonatorum (neonatal conjunctivitis) caused by maternal transmission of Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis. It is a key immediate newborn care intervention.

text: What is the primary purpose of Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) for low birthweight (<2.5 kg) and stable preterm newborns?

options.A: To teach the mother how to bathe the baby
options.B: To provide continuous skin-to-skin contact for temperature regulation and encourage breastfeeding
options.C: To isolate the baby from family members to prevent infection
options.D: To assess the newborn's motor reflexes

explanation: KMC provides continuous skin-to-skin contact between mother (or caregiver) and baby, which acts as a natural incubator to prevent hypothermia, stimulates breast milk production, promotes early bonding, and reduces neonatal infection risk.

text: A newborn is assessed 1 minute after birth and shows: heart rate of 95 beats per minute, slow and irregular breathing, active flexion of limbs, grimacing when nasal suction is applied, and a pink body with blue hands and feet. What is this baby's APGAR score?
explanation: APGAR scoring: Heart rate (<100) = 1; Respiratory effort (slow/irregular) = 1; Muscle tone (active flexion) = 2; Reflex irritability (grimace) = 1; Color (body pink, blue extremities) = 1. Total score = 1+1+2+1+1 = 6.

text: What is the current FMOH guideline for routine umbilical cord care in newborns to prevent neonatal sepsis and tetanus?

options.A: Applying methylated spirit after every bath
options.B: Applying 4% Chlorhexidine gel/solution daily until the cord separates
options.C: Applying local herbal pastes and keeping it covered
options.D: Leaving the cord completely dry without any application

explanation: The FMOH recommends the application of 4% Chlorhexidine gel/solution (yielding 7.1% Chlorhexidine digluconate) to the umbilical cord stump daily for the first week to reduce infection and neonatal mortality. Traditional practices like using methylated spirit, cow dung, or local herbs are discouraged.

text: Why is it critical to administer a single dose of Vitamin K intramuscularly to a newborn within 1 hour of birth?

options.A: To boost the immune system against tuberculosis
options.B: To prevent Vitamin K Deficiency Bleeding (VKDB), also known as hemorrhagic disease of the newborn
options.C: To prevent physiological jaundice of the newborn
options.D: To stimulate the production of thyroid hormones

explanation: Newborns have minimal stores of Vitamin K and a sterile gut that cannot synthesize it. Vitamin K is essential for the synthesis of clotting factors; its deficiency can lead to life-threatening bleeding (VKDB) in the brain or intestines. A single IM dose of 1 mg (or 0.5 mg for preterms) is standard at birth.

text: Which of the following is classified as a critical newborn danger sign that requires immediate referral to a hospital by a CHEW?

options.A: Sleeping for 3 hours between feeds
options.B: Passing yellowish stools 4 times a day
options.C: Fast breathing of 64 breaths per minute at rest
options.D: Slight peeling of the skin on the hands and feet

explanation: Fast breathing (>= 60 breaths/minute) is a major danger sign indicating possible neonatal pneumonia or sepsis. Other signs include poor feeding/inability to suck, convulsions, lethargy, chest indrawing, fever, and hypothermia.

text: A mother who delivered 4 days ago at a Primary Health Clinic is concerned about a reddish vaginal discharge. How should the CHEW classify this discharge and counsel the mother?

options.A: Lochia rubra, which is normal for the first 3 to 4 days postpartum
options.B: Lochia serosa, which indicates mild uterine infection
options.C: Secondary postpartum haemorrhage, requiring blood transfusion
options.D: Lochia alba, which should be white and foul-smelling

explanation: Lochia rubra is the normal, red, blood-stained discharge containing decidual and fetal debris, lasting for the first 3-4 days after birth. The CHEW should reassure the mother that this is a normal physiological process and monitor for foul smell or excess volume.

text: A woman who delivered 30 minutes ago at a Primary Health Clinic is bleeding heavily. On abdominal examination, the CHEW finds that her uterus is soft, boggy, and palpated above the umbilicus. What is the immediate first-line action?

options.A: Refer the patient immediately without touching the abdomen
options.B: Perform continuous uterine massage until the uterus contracts and becomes firm
options.C: Administer 600 mcg of oral Misoprostol only and wait for 1 hour
options.D: Insert a vaginal pack to block the bleeding

explanation: The most common cause of primary postpartum haemorrhage is uterine atony. Rubbing up the fundus (uterine massage) is the immediate first-line physical intervention to stimulate uterine contraction and stop bleeding. It should be accompanied by administering uterotonics like Oxytocin.

text: In community settings where oxytocin is not available, what is the FMOH-recommended dosage of oral Misoprostol for the prevention of postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) immediately after the birth of the baby?

options.A: 200 mcg
options.B: 400 mcg
options.C: 600 mcg
options.D: 800 mcg

explanation: For prevention of PPH in settings where oxytocin is unavailable, the FMOH guidelines recommend administering 600 mcg of Misoprostol (typically 3 tablets of 200 mcg each) orally immediately after the birth of the baby, after ruling out a second twin.

text: A mother presents to the clinic 8 days postpartum complaining of high fever (39°C), severe lower abdominal pain, and foul-smelling vaginal discharge. On examination, she has a rapid pulse and marked uterine tenderness. What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.A: Malaria in the postpartum period
options.B: Puerperal sepsis
options.C: Urinary tract infection
options.D: Normal postpartum lochia transition

explanation: Puerperal sepsis is a severe bacterial infection of the genital tract occurring within 42 days of delivery. Key indicators are fever, foul-smelling lochia, and uterine tenderness, requiring urgent broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy and fluid management.

text: During the management of postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) due to uterine atony at a Primary Health Centre, if bleeding continues despite uterine massage and administration of Oxytocin 10 IU IM, what is the next step according to emergency protocols before referral?

options.A: Give another 10 IU of Oxytocin IM every 5 minutes
options.B: Perform bimanual uterine compression and administer Misoprostol 800 mcg sublingually
options.C: Perform an immediate emergency hysterectomy
options.D: Wait for 30 minutes to see if the bleeding slows down

explanation: When initial management fails, secondary measures include bimanual uterine compression (external or internal), administering a second-line uterotonic such as 800 mcg Misoprostol sublingually, starting IV fluids, and preparing for urgent referral.

text: A stable preterm infant weighing 1.7 kg is receiving Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) at home. The CHEW is conducting a home visit. Which of the following findings indicates that KMC must be suspended and the baby referred urgently to the hospital?

options.A: The baby's body temperature is 36.8°C
options.B: The baby sleeps for 2.5 hours continuously after feeding
options.C: The baby has chest indrawing and grunting sounds during breathing
options.D: The baby passes soft, yellow stools after every feed

explanation: Chest indrawing and grunting are signs of respiratory distress and potential sepsis, indicating the infant is no longer stable and needs advanced clinical care, including oxygen therapy and IV antibiotics.

text: A CHEW is evaluating a mother at her 2-week postnatal contact. What type of lochia should be present in a healthy mother, and what are its characteristics?

options.A: Lochia rubra, which is dark red and contains blood clots
options.B: Lochia serosa, which is pinkish-brown and watery
options.C: Lochia alba, which is yellowish-white or cream-colored
options.D: No discharge should be present by the second week

explanation: Lochia transitions from rubra (days 1-3) to serosa (days 4-10) and finally to lochia alba (days 11 to 3-6 weeks), which is a yellowish-white, creamy discharge consisting of leukocytes, decidual cells, and mucus. Its presence at 2 weeks is completely normal.

text: During neonatal resuscitation at birth, if a newborn's heart rate remains below 60 beats per minute after 30 seconds of effective positive pressure ventilation (PPV), what is the next immediate step?

options.A: Continue PPV alone for another 5 minutes
options.B: Initiate chest compressions coordinated with PPV at a 3:1 ratio
options.C: Administer high-dose adrenaline intravenously immediately
options.D: Immerse the baby in cold water to stimulate the heart

explanation: Under neonatal resuscitation guidelines, if the heart rate is <60 bpm after 30 seconds of effective ventilation, chest compressions must be started and coordinated with ventilation in a 3:1 ratio (3 compressions to 1 breath).

text: During a family planning counseling session, a CHEW uses the 'GATHER' framework. What does the letter 'T' stand for in this acronym?

options.A: Test for pregnancy
options.B: Tell the client about different family planning methods
options.C: Teach the client how to use calendar tracking
options.D: Treat any side effects immediately

explanation: GATHER stands for: Greet the client, Ask about their needs, Tell them about available methods (their advantages, disadvantages, and side effects), Help them choose, Explain how to use the chosen method, and Return for follow-up.

text: Which of the following family planning methods is classified as a permanent surgical method of contraception?

options.A: Intrauterine Device (IUD)
options.B: Bilateral Tubal Ligation
options.C: Depo-Provera injection
options.D: Subdermal implants

explanation: Bilateral Tubal Ligation (for women) and Vasectomy (for men) are permanent, surgical contraceptive methods that involve severing or blocking the fallopian tubes or vas deferens. IUDs, injections, and implants are reversible methods.

text: What is the primary mechanism of action of Combined Oral Contraceptive (COC) pills in preventing pregnancy?

options.A: Destroying sperm in the vagina
options.B: Preventing the release of an egg (inhibiting ovulation)
options.C: Preventing implantation of a fertilized egg by causing infection
options.D: Creating a physical barrier in the cervix

explanation: COCs contain estrogen and progestogen, which work together to suppress the release of Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH), thereby inhibiting LH and FSH secretion and preventing ovulation.

text: A client requests the injectable contraceptive Depo-Provera (DMPA). What is the standard duration of contraceptive protection provided by a single dose of this injection?

options.A: 4 weeks (1 month)
options.B: 8 weeks (2 months)
options.C: 13 weeks (3 months)
options.D: 26 weeks (6 months)

explanation: Depo-Provera (Medroxyprogesterone acetate) is administered intramuscularly or subcutaneously and provides highly effective contraception for 13 weeks (approximately 3 months). Re-injection should occur every 12 to 13 weeks.

text: According to the WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC), which of the following clinical conditions is an absolute contraindication (MEC Category 4) for Combined Oral Contraceptive (COC) use?

options.A: History of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or pulmonary embolism
options.B: Well-controlled mild hypertension
options.C: Controlled diabetes mellitus without vascular disease
options.D: Mild obesity (BMI of 30 kg/m²)

explanation: Estrogen in COCs increases the synthesis of clotting factors, elevating the risk of thromboembolism. A history of DVT or pulmonary embolism is MEC Category 4 (unacceptable health risk, should not be used).

text: A postpartum mother wishes to use the Lactational Amenorrhea Method (LAM) for family planning. What three conditions must be met for LAM to be highly effective?

options.A: Baby is under 12 months, mother is menstruating, and baby receives formula at night
options.B: Baby is under 6 months, mother has not resumed menstruation, and baby is exclusively breastfed
options.C: Mother is breastfeeds at least twice a day, uses condoms, and baby is under 6 months
options.D: Baby is exclusively breastfed, mother has resumed menstruation, and baby is under 9 months
